survey.title: Diffusion Models: A Comprehensive Survey of Methods and Applications
survey.abstract: Diffusion models are a class of deep generative models that have shown impressive results on various tasks. This survey provides a comprehensive review of diffusion models from three perspectives: model formulation, model variants guided by sampling speed and likelihood optimization, and downstream applications.

ddpm.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
ddpm.highlight: First work to demonstrate that diffusion models can generate high-quality images competitive with GANs using a simple denoising objective.
ddpm.contribution: Introduced the DDPM formulation using a Markov chain to gradually add noise and learned reverse process with U-Net. Proposed a simplified training objective (noise prediction) that achieves better sample quality than the full variational lower bound.

ablationStudy.finding: L_simple (noise prediction) significantly outperforms L_vlb for sample quality
Cosine schedule slightly outperforms linear schedule on high-resolution images
Increasing depth/width consistently improves FID up to ~100M parameters

ddpm.pipeline:
graph LR
    A[Input Image x_0] -->|q| B[Add Noise x_t]
    B --> C[U-Net]
    D[Timestep t] --> E[Time Embedding]
    E --> C
    C -->|Predict| F[Noise epsilon]
    F --> G[L2 Loss]
    G --> H[Gradient Update]
    H --> C

methodSteps.title: Forward Diffusion
methodSteps.description: Define a Markov chain that gradually adds Gaussian noise to data: q(x_t | x_{t-1}) = N(x_t; sqrt(1-beta_t) x_{t-1}, beta_t I). After T steps, x_T becomes pure Gaussian noise.

methodSteps.title: Reverse Process
methodSteps.description: Learn the reverse distribution p_theta(x_{t-1} | x_t) parameterized by a U-Net. The model predicts either the noise epsilon or the original data x_0.

methodSteps.title: Simplified Objective
methodSteps.description: Instead of the full variational lower bound, use L_simple = E[||epsilon - epsilon_theta(x_t, t)||^2] which is easier to optimize and yields better samples.

methodSteps.title: Sampling
methodSteps.description: Starting from pure noise x_T ~ N(0, I), iteratively denoise using the learned reverse process for T=1000 steps to obtain a generated image x_0.

keyComponents.name: U-Net Backbone
keyComponents.description: Convolutional encoder-decoder with skip connections. Downsampling blocks extract multi-scale features; upsampling blocks reconstruct the denoised output.

keyComponents.name: Time Embedding
keyComponents.description: Sinusoidal position encoding transformed by a small MLP, injected into every residual block via adaptive group normalization to condition the model on the noise level.

keyComponents.name: Self-Attention
keyComponents.description: Multi-head attention inserted at 16x16 resolution to capture long-range spatial dependencies in the feature maps.

keyComponents.name: Skip Connections
keyComponents.description: Residual connections between corresponding encoder and decoder layers preserve fine-grained spatial information essential for high-quality reconstruction.

equations.label: Forward Process
equations.formula: q(x_t | x_{t-1}) = N(x_t; sqrt(1 - beta_t) x_{t-1}, beta_t I)

equations.label: Reverse Process
equations.formula: p_theta(x_{t-1} | x_t) = N(x_{t-1}; mu_theta(x_t, t), Sigma_theta(x_t, t))

iddpm.title: Improved Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
iddpm.highlight: Improved DDPM with learned variance, cosine noise schedule, and architectural enhancements. Achieved new SOTA FID on ImageNet.
iddpm.contribution: Proposed cosine noise schedule that prevents abrupt changes in signal-to-noise ratio. Introduced learned variance with a hybrid training objective. Added architectural improvements: scaling residual branches and attention at 16x16 resolution.

ablationStudy.finding: Hybrid objective (L_simple + L_vlb) enables both good sample quality and likelihood
Cosine schedule reduces high-frequency artifacts compared to linear
Attention at 16x16 improves ImageNet results more than CIFAR-10

stable-diffusion.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
stable-diffusion.highlight: Latent Diffusion Model (LDM) that runs diffusion in a compressed latent space, enabling high-resolution image generation on consumer GPUs.
stable-diffusion.contribution: Proposed performing diffusion in the latent space of a pretrained VAE, reducing computational cost by orders of magnitude. Introduced cross-attention conditioning for flexible text and image guidance. Released Stable Diffusion as an open-source model.

ablationStudy.finding: f=8 VAE compression provides best quality/compute tradeoff
Cross-attention outperforms simple concatenation for text guidance
Filtering LAION by aesthetics significantly improves visual quality

architecture.crossAttention: Q/K/V projections at each U-Net level

stable-diffusion.pipeline:
graph TD
    A[Text Prompt] -->|CLIP| B[Text Embedding]
    C[Random Noise z_T] --> D[U-Net]
    B -->|Cross-Attn| D
    E[Timestep t] -->|Time Embed| D
    D -->|Predict Noise| F[Denoised z_{t-1}]
    F -->|Repeat T steps| D
    F --> G[VAE Decoder]
    G --> H[Generated Image x_0]

methodSteps.title: VAE Encoding
methodSteps.description: A pretrained KL-regularized VAE compresses images into a 4-channel latent space with 8x spatial downsampling (512x512 -> 64x64). The encoder is frozen during diffusion training.

methodSteps.title: Text Encoding
methodSteps.description: Text prompts are encoded using a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 text encoder into 77-token embeddings, which serve as conditioning for the diffusion model.

methodSteps.title: Latent Diffusion
methodSteps.description: Diffusion operates entirely in the compressed latent space. A U-Net predicts the noise epsilon given the noisy latent z_t, timestep t, and text embeddings via cross-attention layers.

methodSteps.title: VAE Decoding
methodSteps.description: After T denoising steps, the final latent z_0 is decoded back to pixel space by the VAE decoder to produce the high-resolution output image.

keyComponents.name: VAE Encoder/Decoder
keyComponents.description: Pretrained KL-regularized autoencoder that compresses images to 1/64th the pixel count (4 channels at 1/8 resolution). Enables training on latent tensors instead of full images.

keyComponents.name: U-Net with Cross-Attention
keyComponents.description: Standard U-Net backbone augmented with transformer-style cross-attention blocks that inject text conditioning into the diffusion process at multiple resolutions.

keyComponents.name: CLIP Text Encoder
keyComponents.description: Frozen OpenAI CLIP ViT-L/14 model that encodes natural language prompts into semantically rich embeddings aligned with visual representations.

keyComponents.name: Classifier-Free Guidance
keyComponents.description: During sampling, interpolates between conditional and unconditional predictions to boost prompt adherence. Scale typically set to 7.5.

dit.title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers
dit.highlight: Replaced U-Net with a Vision Transformer (DiT) and showed that scaling model size and compute predictably improves diffusion model performance.
dit.contribution: Demonstrated that Transformer-based diffusion models (DiT) can outperform U-Net baselines when scaled. Found that model compute (Gflops) is a strong predictor of FID across architectures. Achieved SOTA on ImageNet with DiT-XL/2.

ablationStudy.finding: DiT-XL/2 outperforms all U-Net variants at same compute budget
FID scales predictably as a power law with model Gflops
Smaller patches (2x2) yield better quality but require more compute

uvit.title: All are Worth Words: A ViT Backbone for Diffusion Models
uvit.highlight: A U-ViT architecture that combines Transformer with long skip connections, showing that shallow and wide designs work well for diffusion.
uvit.contribution: Proposed U-ViT with long skip connections between shallow and deep layers for diffusion. Showed that for diffusion, shallow-and-wide ViT outperforms deep-and-narrow ones. Achieved strong results on unconditional and conditional image generation.

ablationStudy.finding: Long skip connections improve convergence speed and final FID
Shallow-and-wide (13 layers, 1024 dim) outperforms deep-and-narrow

ncsn.title: Generative Modeling by Estimating Gradients of the Data Distribution
ncsn.highlight: Introduced Noise Conditional Score Networks (NCSN), using score matching with multiple noise levels for image generation.
ncsn.contribution: Proposed estimating the score function (gradient of log density) using denoising score matching. Introduced annealed Langevin dynamics sampling with multiple noise levels. Demonstrated competitive image generation quality.

ablationStudy.finding: Multiple noise levels crucial; single level fails to cover all data modes
Annealed step schedule outperforms fixed step size for Langevin dynamics

flow-matching.title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling
flow-matching.highlight: A simulation-free approach to training continuous normalizing flows by regressing vector fields, enabling direct optimization without ODE simulation.
flow-matching.contribution: Proposed Flow Matching as a simulation-free training objective for Continuous Normalizing Flows (CNFs). Showed that conditional flow matching with Gaussian paths is equivalent to diffusion models but with a simpler formulation. Enabled training CNFs at scale.

ablationStudy.finding: Optimal transport paths provide better training stability than diffusion paths
Removing ODE simulation during training reduces cost without hurting NLL

rectified-flow.title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data with Rectified Flow
rectified-flow.highlight: Introduced Rectified Flow, an ODE-based generative model that learns nearly straight trajectories, enabling fast one-step generation.
rectified-flow.contribution: Proposed rectification procedure that straightens the flow trajectory while preserving marginal distributions. Showed that straight flows enable high-quality one-step generation. Applied to image generation and domain transfer tasks.

ablationStudy.finding: Single reflow step significantly straightens trajectory; diminishing returns after 2 steps
Rectified flow achieves near multi-step quality with just 1 sampling step

ddim.title: Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models
ddim.highlight: Showed that DDPM can use non-Markovian diffusion processes, enabling deterministic sampling with 10-50x fewer steps.
ddim.contribution: Proposed a class of non-Markovian diffusion processes that share the same training objective as DDPM. Introduced deterministic sampling (DDIM) that achieves comparable quality with 10-50 steps instead of 1000. Enabled meaningful latent interpolation.

ablationStudy.finding: FID plateaus around 50 steps; 10 steps still yields reasonable quality
eta=0 (deterministic) slightly outperforms stochastic sampling at low steps

dpm-solver.title: DPM-Solver: A Fast ODE Solver for Diffusion Probabilistic Model Sampling in Around 10 Steps
dpm-solver.highlight: A dedicated high-order ODE solver for diffusion sampling that achieves high-quality results in 10-20 steps, orders of magnitude faster than DDPM.
dpm-solver.contribution: Derived that diffusion sampling can be formulated as solving an ODE. Proposed DPM-Solver with first/second/third-order methods. Achieved near-SOTA FID with only 10-20 function evaluations.

ablationStudy.finding: Third-order solver achieves best step/quality tradeoff; higher orders unstable
Log-uniform timestep schedule outperforms uniform for all orders

classifier-free.title: Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance
classifier-free.highlight: Replaced classifier guidance with a simpler unconditional training approach, avoiding the need for a separate classifier and achieving better sample quality.
classifier-free.contribution: Proposed jointly training conditional and unconditional diffusion models by randomly dropping conditioning. Showed that guidance can be applied by interpolating between conditional and unconditional scores. Eliminated need for adversarially robust classifiers.

ablationStudy.finding: 10% unconditional dropout provides good guidance strength without hurting base quality
Scale=2-3 provides best quality/diversity tradeoff; higher scales oversaturate

consistency-models.title: Consistency Models
consistency-models.highlight: A new family of generative models that support single-step generation while allowing iterative refinement, trained by distilling pretrained diffusion models.
consistency-models.contribution: Introduced Consistency Models that learn to map any point on a diffusion trajectory to its origin. Supports both distillation from pretrained models and standalone training. Achieved one-step generation with quality approaching multi-step diffusion.

ablationStudy.finding: Distillation converges faster and achieves better one-step FID
Consistency models support iterative refinement with diminishing returns after 2 steps

dalle-2.title: Hierarchical Text-Conditional Image Generation with CLIP Latents
dalle-2.highlight: DALL-E 2: A two-stage model using CLIP embeddings and diffusion decoders to generate photorealistic images from text captions.
dalle-2.contribution: Proposed unCLIP: a prior network generates CLIP image embeddings from text, and a diffusion decoder generates images from these embeddings. Introduced classifier-free guidance and upsampling diffusion models for high resolution.

ablationStudy.finding: Diffusion prior outperforms AR prior on both caption similarity and diversity
Two-stage upsampling (64->256->1024) critical for high-res photorealism

imagen.title: Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Deep Language Understanding
imagen.highlight: Imagen: Showed that large frozen language models (T5-XXL) are surprisingly effective text encoders for text-to-image diffusion, outperforming CLIP.
imagen.contribution: Demonstrated that frozen T5-XXL outperforms CLIP as text encoder for diffusion. Proposed Efficient U-Net with attention pooling and cross-attention. Introduced DrawBench benchmark for text-to-image evaluation.

ablationStudy.finding: T5-XXL > T5-Large > CLIP in both FID and caption alignment
Scaling from 10M to 460M pairs monotonically improves quality

sdxl.title: SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion Models for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
sdxl.highlight: Stable Diffusion XL: A significantly larger latent diffusion model with a second text encoder, micro-conditioning, and a refinement model.
sdxl.contribution: Scaled U-Net to 2.6B parameters with cross-attention. Added OpenCLIP-ViT/G as second text encoder. Introduced size and crop-conditioning for better training data utilization. Released a separate refinement diffusion model.

ablationStudy.finding: OpenCLIP+CLIP combination improves prompt following vs either alone
SDEdit-based refinement improves local details but not global composition

sd-turbo.title: Adversarial Diffusion Distillation
sd-turbo.highlight: SD-Turbo/SDXL-Turbo: Achieved real-time single-step image generation by combining score distillation with an adversarial loss.
sd-turbo.contribution: Proposed Adversarial Diffusion Distillation (ADD) that combines score distillation with adversarial training. Achieved high-quality single-step generation. Applied to both SD and SDXL base models.

ablationStudy.finding: Score distillation alone leads to mode collapse; adversarial loss restores diversity
DINOv2 features more stable than raw pixels for discrimination
